title: Microsoft Teams: third-party synthetic audio and video detection in meetings
summary: Hold: Microsoft now documents the Teams admin center detection settings and organizer response workflow that this briefing reports as undocumented. The briefing also needs to distinguish public and private preview, acknowledge provider-side licensing prerequisites, and complete the app allow/block path.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Teams is adding synthetic audio and video detection integrations with certified third-party providers.
claims.quote: Organizations can enhance meeting security with synthetic audio and video detection solutions provided by certified third-party providers.

claims.claim: The third-party provider, rather than Teams, performs the synthetic media analysis.
claims.quote: Important: Synthetic media detection is performed by the third-party provider.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Teams supplies integration and in-meeting experiences and controls for surfacing and acting on provider signals.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams provides the platform integration and experiences for surfacing and acting on detection signals from supported providers.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Scope: Prerequisites; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft asks administrators to evaluate a provider, deploy its app through Manage apps, grant permissions and configure meeting policies.
claims.quote: administrators should evaluate and select a supported detection provider, deploy the provider app through Manage apps in the Teams admin center, grant required permissions, and configure applicable Teams meeting policies.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Third-party detection requires administrator configuration, so it is admin-opt-in and does not start merely because the feature arrives.
claims.quote: To use third-party Synthetic Audio and Video Detection in Microsoft Teams, administrators should evaluate and select a supported detection provider, deploy the provider app through Manage apps in the Teams admin center, grant required permissions, and configure applicable Teams meeting policies.

claims.claim: The Graph beta reportSyntheticMedia action lets a certified detection bot admitted to a meeting flag a participant's stream as synthetic.
claims.quote: This action is intended for certified third-party audio and video synthetic media detection bots admitted to the meeting call. The detection bot calls this action to flag a participant whose stream it identifies as AI-generated or synthetic media.

claims.claim: The Graph detection result is propagated to all participants through roster updates.
claims.quote: The detection result is propagated to all participants via roster updates.

claims.where: controls[0].api; What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy-name> -SyntheticMediaDetection Enabled -SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId <supported-provider-app-id> permits detection with a supported provider's Teams App ID.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "SyntheticDetectionPolicy" -SyntheticMediaDetection Enabled -SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId "<supported-provider-app-id>"

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope: Users and policies; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The detection setting governs meetings organized by users assigned the meeting policy.
claims.quote: Controls whether synthetic audio/video detection is permitted for meetings organized by users assigned this policy.

claims.claim: SyntheticMediaDetection Disabled disables detection regardless of the configured provider.
claims.quote: In Example 5, the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy cmdlet disables synthetic audio/video detection for meetings organized by users assigned this policy, regardless of the configured detection provider.

claims.claim: Disabling detection leaves SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId unchanged.
claims.quote: The SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId value is unchanged.

claims.claim: SyntheticMediaDetection defaults to Enabled, permitting detection when a configured provider is available.
claims.quote: Enabled: Permits synthetic media detection when a configured detection provider is available. This is the default value.

claims.claim: SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId defaults to the zero GUID, which does not select a third-party provider.
claims.quote: The default value, the zero GUID (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000), selects no provider when Microsoft Detection is unavailable, or Microsoft Detection when it is available. It does not select a third-party provider.

claims.claim: Saving a policy does not validate provider support, and an incorrect or unsupported App ID can prevent the bot joining.
claims.quote: Successfully saving the policy does not guarantee that the App ID identifies a supported provider or that the detection bot can join meetings. An incorrect or unsupported App ID can prevent the detection bot from joining eligible meetings.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a Teams admin center setting for detection permission and provider selection.
claims.quote: Under Meeting protection, select a provider from the Synthetic audio and video detection provider dropdown list. ... The Turn on synthetic audio and video protection setting appears and is on by default.
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].ui null with surface 'Teams admin center', path 'Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting protection > Synthetic audio and video detection provider > Turn on synthetic audio and video protection', and docs https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/third-party-synthetic-audio-video-detection-meetings. Replace the repeated UI absence and corresponding open question with that documented preview route, and cite the page.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps is the complete path to the app allow/block control.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.
claims.fix: Change controls[1].ui.path to 'Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block'. End the rollout instruction at 'app > Allow'; retain the existing prose route ending in 'app > Block' for blocking.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <value> is the MicrosoftTeams cmdlet surface for changing app state.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true

claims.claim: The Update-M365TeamsApp reference describes an example using -IsBlocked $true as unblocking.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true ... Unblocks Bookings app

claims.claim: Some apps are Blocked by publisher until administrators complete publisher configuration.
claims.quote: Before an admin allows an agent or app, it shows as Blocked by publisher in the admin center. Before you allow it for users, follow the publisher's guidance to configure it.

claims.claim: App allow/block governs provider app availability and is not sufficient by itself to enable detection.
claims.quote: App availability and required consent must remain in place for the integration to function. A provider appearing in the dropdown doesn't confirm that these prerequisites are met.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/third-party-synthetic-audio-video-detection-meetings to sources. Replace 'not confirmed as the only gate' with 'App availability, required consent, provider-side activation and meeting policy configuration are separate prerequisites.'

claims.claim: Reality Defender RealMeeting has a Microsoft 365 App Certification program page.
claims.quote: # Reality Defender RealMeeting ... Publisher Attestation: The information on this page is based on a self-assessment report provided by the app developer

claims.claim: Pindrop Pulse has a Microsoft 365 App Certification page.
claims.quote: # Pindrop Pulse ... Certification information ... APPLICATION SECURITY ... PASS

claims.claim: Reality Defender's listing declares the Calls.AccessMedia.All application permission for real-time audio and video access.
claims.quote: Calls.AccessMedia.All | application | The app is a meeting-recording bot, so it needs Graph to join Teams meetings and access the real-time audio and video media in order to run authenticity and deepfake analysis.

claims.claim: The Reality Defender listing is developer self-assessment information whose accuracy Microsoft does not guarantee.
claims.quote: The information on this page is based on a self-assessment report provided by the app developer on the security, compliance, and data handling practices followed by this app. Microsoft makes no guarantees regarding the accuracy of the information.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Prerequisites; Governance controls
claims.claim: A third-party bot needs the meeting tenant administrator to grant Calls.ReportSyntheticMedia.All application permission before reporting detections.
claims.quote: Third-party bots can invoke this action only when the meeting tenant administrator grants the app the Calls.ReportSyntheticMedia.All application permission.

claims.claim: SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents is a Defender advanced hunting table for Teams synthetic media detections.
claims.quote: The SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents table in the advanced hunting schema contains details about synthetic media (deepfake) detection events in Microsoft Teams in your organization.

claims.claim: The detection events table is populated from Microsoft Defender for Office 365 records.
claims.quote: This advanced hunting table is populated by records from Microsoft Defender for Office 365.

claims.claim: The table contains data only when an approved detection engine is used.
claims.quote: This table contains data only if you're using an approved detection engine: Microsoft or a third-party engine.

claims.claim: Learn identifies GetReal, Pindrop, Reality Defender and Resemble AI as approved engines for the detection events table.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Teams synthetic media detection GetReal Pindrop Reality Defender Resemble approved engines. Opened SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents, the feature overview, both cited provider listings and Defender for Office 365 support for Teams; none lists these four approved engines.
claims.fix: Remove 'including GetReal, Pindrop, Reality Defender and Resemble AI'. Retain the documented statement that the table requires an approved Microsoft or third-party detection engine.

claims.claim: Detection events can identify flagged users and meetings.
claims.quote: DetectedUserDisplayName ... Display name of the user flagged as using synthetic media ... SourceContextName ... Name of the source (for example, the meeting, file, or email name)

claims.claim: Learn has no overview page for this feature, leaving the participant experience documented only by the roadmap and provider pages.
claims.quote: Certified third-party synthetic audio and video detection in Microsoft Teams meetings (Preview) ... In public preview, detection results are surfaced through the provider's experience.
claims.fix: Replace the absence sentence with 'Microsoft Learn now has a feature overview: detection results use the provider experience in public preview, while native Teams detection alerts, participant indicators and associated actions are separately in private preview.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/third-party-synthetic-audio-video-detection-meetings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a provider-independent Teams response workflow.
claims.quote: This experience is available only in private preview. ... From the alert or the roster, the organizer can: Remove the flagged participant from the meeting. Mark as not a concern ... Teams doesn't remove participants automatically.
claims.fix: Replace the absence with 'In private preview, the organizer can Remove a flagged participant or select Mark as not a concern from the alert or roster; Teams does not remove participants automatically.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/third-party-synthetic-audio-video-detection-meetings and remove the open question asking which provider-independent actions exist.

claims.claim: Reality Defender's publisher-attested listing says hosts can rescan a participant or end the meeting.
claims.quote: Hosts can rescan a participant or end the meeting if manipulation is detected.

claims.claim: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy at a time.
claims.quote: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy and one events policy at a time.

claims.claim: Users receive the global meeting policy unless a custom policy is created and assigned.
claims.quote: Users get the global policy unless you create and assign a custom policy.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing for the feature is wholly unpublished, represented by licensing.model unknown.
claims.quote: Each provider has its own licensing, service activation, data handling, and support model. Contact the provider directly to purchase or activate its service.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'add-on' for the separately licensed provider service. Replace the blanket licensing absence in the notes, summary, body and cost rationale with 'The provider supplies the service under its own licensing and activation model. Complete any provider-side licensing or service activation before setup; a detection-specific Teams licence, price or meter is not yet published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/third-party-synthetic-audio-video-detection-meetings. Do not infer a provider price or change the cost rating solely from unpublished prices.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Providers may analyze meeting audio/video, and Microsoft asks administrators to review provider terms, data handling and compliance documentation before enabling.
claims.quote: Certified third-party providers may analyze meeting audio/video signals for synthetic media detection. Review provider terms, data handling, and compliance documentation before enabling.

claims.claim: The two cited cmdlet reference pages themselves do not specify the administrator role needed to run them.
claims.quote: Searched the fetched Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy text for role and administrator; read Update-M365TeamsApp. Neither reference specifies a role. The separate feature overview does specify Teams Administrator or higher for app and meeting-policy management.

claims.claim: The App ID parameter documentation refers to Microsoft Detection when available.
claims.quote: The default value, the zero GUID (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000), selects no provider when Microsoft Detection is unavailable, or Microsoft Detection when it is available.

claims.claim: The roadmap's Rolling out status and General Availability release phase are reported without the feature documentation's preview qualifications.
claims.quote: This feature is currently in public preview. ... Native Teams detection alerts, participant indicators, and associated actions are available separately in private preview.
claims.fix: Retain the roadmap status, target and release phases. Add 'Learn describes the feature as public preview, with native Teams detection alerts, participant indicators and associated actions separately in private preview; UI labels and supported scenarios can change before general availability.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/third-party-synthetic-audio-video-detection-meetings and qualify the newly documented UI and organizer actions as preview.
